correctness.rationale: The classification follows from P=[A 0;C B], row sparsity, B=A^[2] and P²=P. A is a rooted weighted partial idempotent map with binomial(n,r)(1+r(q−1))^(n−r) possibilities, B has rank r, and the two unconstrained off-diagonal blocks of C give q^(2r(n−r)). Hence exact image rank 2r and image E_r. Log weights have strictly concave second difference ≤−4 ln q; uniform Stirling/Taylor expansion within O(ln n) of n/2 gives center mu_n and sharp prefactor K_n; concentration and tail domination prove total variation and total count asymptotics. The verify.py direct finite-field enumeration produced matching rank histograms for (1,2),(2,2),(3,2),(2,3),(2,4) and finite-dimensional Gaussian comparisons.

originality.rationale: Elduque–Labra arXiv:1602.01590 Corollary 2.6 explicitly gives the underlying direct-sum evolution-algebra class. Omirov–Rozikov–Velasco arXiv:1711.05030 studies nilpotent evolution-algebra classification and provides the 2017 motivating source. Boudi et al. arXiv:2006.14460 and Kaygorodov et al. arXiv:2610.22248 address natural families, structure, automorphisms, and idempotent elements. Sen arXiv:1909.05887 treats combinatorial idempotent functions; that ingredient does not itself count free central blocks or give their rank asymptotics. Targeted search of published research records and web literature did not identify the claimed exact retract rank formula or drifting Gaussian law. Priority is provisional.
residual_risks: The algebra is a direct sum and its idempotent quotient map is a weighted rooted partial transformation; unexamined generalized transformation-semigroup formulas could cover the exact count.

value.rationale: Retractions and their image ranks are natural invariants of an algebra. The theorem gives their complete infinite-family census and isomorphism types, plus a sharp moving-theta total count and a genuinely logarithmically displaced discrete-Gaussian typical rank. Neither general structure classification nor plain rooted-function enumeration quantifies field-linear central-extension splitting fibers or this shifted rank law.
